claim: RAF kinase inhibitors can, under certain conditions, increase RAF kinase signaling.
source: RAF kinase inhibitors can, under certain conditions, increase RAF kinase signaling.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the paradoxical activation phenomenon.

claim: The process of RAF kinase inhibitors increasing RAF kinase signaling is commonly referred to as 'paradoxical activation' (PA).
source: This process, which is commonly referred to as 'paradoxical activation' (PA), is incompletely understood.
evidence: This statement defines the terminology used in the field.

claim: Paradoxical activation is incompletely understood.
source: This process, which is commonly referred to as 'paradoxical activation' (PA), is incompletely understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Conformational autoinhibition modulation by a RAF inhibitor could be sufficient to create PA.
source: We find that conformational autoinhibition modulation by a RAF inhibitor could be sufficient to create PA.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical modeling presented in the manuscript.

claim: Experimental RAF inhibitor drug dose–response data that characterize PA across different types of RAF inhibitors are best explained by a model that includes RAF inhibitor modulation of three properties: conformational autoinhibition, dimer affinity, and drug binding within the dimer (i.e., negative cooperativity).
source: We find that experimental RAF inhibitor drug dose–response data that characterize PA across different types of RAF inhibitors are best explained by a model that includes RAF inhibitor modulation of three properties: conformational autoinhibition, dimer affinity, and drug binding within the dimer (i.e., negative cooperativity).
evidence: This is a conclusion from fitting the mathematical model to experimental data.

claim: Conformational autoinhibition is a robust mechanism for RAF inhibitor-driven PA based solely on equilibrium dynamics of canonical interactions that comprise RAF signaling and inhibition.
source: Overall, this work establishes conformational autoinhibition as a robust mechanism for RAF inhibitor-driven PA based solely on equilibrium dynamics of canonical interactions that comprise RAF signaling and inhibition.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the theoretical analysis.

claim: Cancer is characterized by a collection of shared phenotypes.
source: Cancer is a disease that is characterized by a collection of shared phenotypes (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011.

claim: Self-sufficiency in pro-growth signals is among the phenotypes that characterize cancer.
source: Among these phenotypes is self-sufficiency in the pro-growth signals that aberrantly drive the continued proliferation of the cancerous cells.
evidence: This is a statement about cancer biology, following from the cited work.

claim: Excessive pro-growth signals in cancer may result from somatic mutations within a proliferation signaling pathway.
source: These excessive pro-growth signals may result from somatic mutations within a proliferation signaling pathway, and they could also result from excessive stimulation of transmembrane receptor proteins.
evidence: This is a statement about mechanisms of cancer signaling.

claim: Excessive pro-growth signals in cancer could result from excessive stimulation of transmembrane receptor proteins.
source: These excessive pro-growth signals may result from somatic mutations within a proliferation signaling pathway, and they could also result from excessive stimulation of transmembrane receptor proteins.
evidence: This is a statement about mechanisms of cancer signaling.

claim: Pro-growth, proliferation signals commonly pass through RAS GTPases (KRAS, NRAS, and HRAS) and RAF kinases (BRAF, CRAF, and ARAF) to initiate the RAF/MEK/ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade.
source: Such pro-growth, proliferation, signals commonly pass through RAS GTPases (KRAS, NRAS, and HRAS) and RAF kinases (BRAF, CRAF, and ARAF) to initiate the RAF/MEK/ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade.
evidence: This is a statement about the RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK signaling pathway.

claim: Pharmacological agents that counteract pro-growth signals have proven to be therapeutically beneficial in cancer.
source: Pharmacological agents that counteract these pro-growth signals have proven to be therapeutically beneficial in cancer.
evidence: This is a general statement about cancer therapeutics.

claim: FDA-approved agents for upstream receptor tyrosine kinases that can drive proliferation through RAS/RAF signaling have proven effective for a variety of cancers.
source: FDA-approved agents for upstream receptor tyrosine kinases that can drive proliferation through RAS/RAF signaling have proven effective for a variety of cancers.
evidence: This is a statement about approved cancer therapies.

claim: EGFR inhibitors (both small molecule and therapeutic antibodies) have established benefit in lung, colorectal, and head and neck adenocarcinomas.
source: For example, EGFR inhibitors (both small molecule and therapeutic antibodies) have established benefit in lung, colorectal, and head and neck adenocarcinomas (Ciardiello and Tortora, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ciardiello and Tortora, 2008.

claim: RAS GTPases have only recently become targetable, although for only one specific somatic mutation (KRAS G12C).
source: Downstream from receptor tyrosine kinases, the RAS GTPases have only recently become targetable, although for only one specific somatic mutation (KRAS G12C) (Skoulidis et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Skoulidis et al., 2021.

claim: Multiple drugs have been developed to inhibit the RAF kinases.
source: Multiple drugs have been developed to inhibit the RAF kinases (Bollag et al., 2010; Nakamura et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2015), and several of these agents have proven clinically valuable for RAF mutant melanoma and colorectal cancer.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Several RAF inhibitor agents have proven clinically valuable for RAF mutant melanoma and colorectal cancer.
source: Multiple drugs have been developed to inhibit the RAF kinases (Bollag et al., 2010; Nakamura et al., 2013; Peng et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2015), and several of these agents have proven clinically valuable for RAF mutant melanoma and colorectal cancer.
evidence: This statement is supported by the citations about RAF inhibitor development.

claim: A drug that successfully inhibits its target protein must also avoid significant effects in non-diseased cells and tissues to be effective.
source: The development of a drug that successfully inhibits its target protein is not sufficient to produce an effective drug. The drug must also avoid significant effects in non-diseased cells and tissues.
evidence: This is a general principle of drug development.

claim: RAF inhibitors were originally hoped to be able to block the transmission of RAS signals.
source: For example, it was originally hoped that RAF inhibitors would be able to block the transmission of RAS signals (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a statement about the original expectations for RAF inhibitors, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: RAF inhibitors were found to amplify RAS signals within the RAF wild-type context through a process now commonly referred to as 'paradoxical activation' (PA).
source: Unexpectedly, RAF inhibitors were found to amplify RAS signals within the RAF wild-type context through a process that is now commonly referred to as 'paradoxical activation' (PA) (Hatzivassiliou et al., 2010; Heidorn et al., 2010; Poulikakos et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: PA is associated with the development of drug-dependent squamous cell carcinomas in a subpopulation of those treated with RAF inhibitors.
source: PA is also associated with the development of drug-dependent squamous cell carcinomas in a subpopulation of those treated with RAF inhibitors (Su et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Su et al., 2012.

claim: The mechanisms driving PA are still not fully understood.
source: Despite numerous studies, the mechanisms driving PA are still not fully understood (Karoulia et al., 2017; Karoulia et al., 2016; Peng et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: A mathematical model of biochemical processes allows one to rigorously analyze what behaviors are possible for a given set of reaction mechanisms.
source: A mathematical model of biochemical processes allows one to rigorously analyze what behaviors are possible for a given set of reaction mechanisms.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of mathematical modeling.

claim: Modeling can lead to mechanism-driven hypotheses for further experimental testing.
source: Modeling can lead to mechanism-driven hypotheses for further experimental testing (Kholodenko, 2015; McFall et al., 2019; Rukhlenko et al., 2018; Stites et al., 2015; Stites et al., 2007; Wofsy et al., 1992).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mathematical models have proven useful for understanding mechanisms of anticancer agents.
source: Some of these mathematical models have proven useful for understanding mechanisms of anticancer agents.
evidence: This is a general statement about the application of mathematical models.

claim: A mathematical model was used to identify the mechanism that explains why colorectal cancer patients with a KRAS G13D mutation benefit from treatment with EGFR inhibitors despite KRAS mutations more commonly causing resistance to EGFR inhibitors.
source: For example, we recently used a mathematical model to identify the mechanism (McFall et al., 2019; McFall et al., 2020; McFall and Stites, 2021) that explains why colorectal cancer patients with a KRAS G13D mutation benefit from treatment with EGFR inhibitors despite KRAS mutations more commonly causing resistance to EGFR inhibitors (De Roock et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: A mechanistic explanation for why colorectal cancer patients with a KRAS G13D mutation benefit from treatment with EGFR inhibitors evaded determination through traditional experimental methods for approximately a decade.
source: These studies are significant because a mechanistic explanation for this high-profile problem evaded determination through traditional experimental methods for approximately a decade.
evidence: This is a statement about the difficulty of solving this problem experimentally.

claim: Mathematical models can complement experimental approaches to provide new understandings to clinically relevant biological systems.
source: Thus, mathematical models can complement experimental approaches to provide new understandings to clinically relevant biological systems.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the value of mathematical modeling.

claim: Some RAF inhibitors have been shown to result in an increased level of RAF dimerization.
source: First, some RAF inhibitors have been shown to result in an increased level of RAF dimerization (Hatzivassiliou et al., 2010; Jin et al., 2017; Karoulia et al., 2016; Lavoie et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Drug-induced dimer potentiation (DP) is commonly thought of as manifesting in a higher affinity between RAF protomers when one (or both) are bound to a RAF inhibitor.
source: This drug-induced dimer potentiation (DP) is commonly thought of as manifesting in a higher affinity between RAF protomers when one (or both) are bound to a RAF inhibitor (Kholodenko, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kholodenko, 2015.

claim: Many RAF inhibitors do not appear capable of binding to both protomers of a RAF dimer equally well.
source: Second, many RAF inhibitors do not appear capable of binding to both protomers of a RAF dimer equally well (Karoulia et al., 2017; Karoulia et al., 2016; Peng et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Only one protomer in a RAF dimer need be signaling competent for RAF signaling to propagate.
source: As only one protomer in a RAF dimer need be signaling competent for RAF signaling to propagate (Heidorn et al., 2010; Hu et al., 2013; Yuan et al., 2018), such negative cooperativity (NC) is posited to result in a reduced ability to fully inhibit RAF signaling.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Negative cooperativity (NC) is posited to result in a reduced ability to fully inhibit RAF signaling.
source: As only one protomer in a RAF dimer need be signaling competent for RAF signaling to propagate (Heidorn et al., 2010; Hu et al., 2013; Yuan et al., 2018), such negative cooperativity (NC) is posited to result in a reduced ability to fully inhibit RAF signaling.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the cited work.

claim: NC is commonly thought of as manifesting in a reduced affinity for the binding of a second RAF inhibitor relative to the affinity with which the first RAF inhibitor bound.
source: This NC is commonly thought of as manifesting in a reduced affinity for the binding of a second RAF inhibitor relative to the affinity with which the first RAF inhibitor bound (Kholodenko, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kholodenko, 2015.

claim: Previous theoretical studies of PA have focused on dimer potentiation and negative cooperativity mechanisms.
source: Previous theoretical studies of PA have focused on these two mechanisms (Kholodenko, 2015; Rukhlenko et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: A mathematical model was developed that describes key regulatory steps in RAF signaling.
source: We developed a mathematical model that describes key regulatory steps in RAF signaling.
evidence: This is a description of the work performed in this study.

claim: The model was developed to follow biochemical and thermodynamic principles.
source: We developed the model to follow biochemical and thermodynamic principles, and we derive the behaviors that logically follow from the RAF regulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This is a description of the modeling approach.

claim: The model includes three different mechanisms that contribute to PA: dimer potentiation, negative cooperativity, and RAF autoinhibitory conformational regulation.
source: Our model includes three different mechanisms that contribute to PA; two have received previous theoretical attention and one (RAF autoinhibitory conformational regulation) has not previously received a mathematical consideration.
evidence: This is a description of the model components.

claim: RAF autoinhibitory conformational regulation has not previously received a mathematical consideration in the context of PA.
source: Our model includes three different mechanisms that contribute to PA; two have received previous theoretical attention and one (RAF autoinhibitory conformational regulation) has not previously received a mathematical consideration.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the work.

claim: The fit model suggests links between the three types of RAF inhibitors and the three mechanisms that contribute to PA.
source: We fit our model to experimental data, and the fit model suggests links between the three types of RAF inhibitors and the three mechanisms that contribute to PA.
evidence: This is a conclusion from fitting the model to data.

claim: All three mechanisms (conformational autoinhibition, dimer potentiation, and negative cooperativity) and their modulation by RAF inhibitor binding are necessary to explain PA.
source: Overall, this study suggests that all three mechanisms and their modulation by RAF inhibitor binding are necessary to explain PA.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study.

claim: The regulation of RAF kinase activation is complex with multiple regulatory steps.
source: The regulation of RAF kinase activation is complex with multiple regulatory steps (Hu et al., 2013; Karoulia et al., 2016; Lavoie and Therrien, 2015; Wellbrock et al., 2004, Brummer and McInnes, 2020), and several of these processes have been described to play a role in PA (Cho et al., 2012; Heidorn et al., 2010; Holderfield et al., 2013; Kondo et al., 2019; McKay et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Several regulatory processes of RAF kinase activation have been described to play a role in PA.
source: The regulation of RAF kinase activation is complex with multiple regulatory steps (Hu et al., 2013; Karoulia et al., 2016; Lavoie and Therrien, 2015; Wellbrock et al., 2004, Brummer and McInnes, 2020), and several of these processes have been described to play a role in PA (Cho et al., 2012; Heidorn et al., 2010; Holderfield et al., 2013; Kondo et al., 2019; McKay et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Conformational changes of the RAF monomer contribute significantly to RAF kinase activation.
source: Conformational changes of the RAF monomer contribute significantly to RAF kinase activation (Jin et al., 2017; Lavoie and Therrien, 2015; Martinez Fiesco et al., 2022; Wellbrock et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In the 'autoinhibited' form, associations between RAF's N-terminus and its kinase domain maintain RAF in an inactive form that does not dimerize.
source: In the 'autoinhibited' form, associations between its N-terminus and its kinase domain maintain RAF in an inactive form that does not dimerize (Cutler et al., 1998; Lavoie and Therrien, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: In the 'non-autoinhibited' form, the kinase domain is no longer occluded, and other regulatory mechanisms contribute to full RAF kinase activation, such as kinase domain conformational changes and dimerization.
source: In the 'non-autoinhibited' form, the kinase domain is no longer occluded, and other regulatory mechanisms contribute to full RAF kinase activation, such as kinase domain conformational changes and dimerization (Lavoie and Therrien, 2015; Lavoie et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: RAF inhibitors tend to promote a net transition to the non-autoinhibited conformation that is bound to RAS-GTP.
source: Recent experimental work reports that RAF inhibitors tend to promote a net transition to the non-autoinhibited conformation that is bound to RAS-GTP (Jin et al., 2017; Karoulia et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent experimental work.

claim: It has previously been suggested that biasing to the non-autoinhibited state may contribute to PA.
source: It has previously been suggested that this biasing to the non-autoinhibited state may contribute to PA (Figure 1B; Jin et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Conformational autoinhibition (CA) has not previously received a theoretical analysis to evaluate whether, and how, it may contribute to PA.
source: However, conformational autoinhibition (CA) has not previously received a theoretical analysis to evaluate whether, and how, it may contribute to PA.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in previous research.

claim: A series of mathematical models were developed that include CA of RAF, NC within a RAF dimer, and RAF DP.
source: We therefore developed a series of mathematical models that include CA of RAF, NC within a RAF dimer, and RAF DP.
evidence: This is a description of the modeling work performed.

claim: Different subsets of the full mechanism were systematically studied to investigate how each contributes to PA.
source: We systematically studied different subsets of the full mechanism to investigate how each contributes to PA.
evidence: This is a description of the modeling approach.

claim: Analytic equations were derived that provide the equilibrium solution for each sub-model.
source: For each sub-model, we derived analytic equations that provide the equilibrium solution for the system.
evidence: This is a description of the mathematical analysis performed.

claim: An analytic expression can be utilized to determine the generality of a result and/or to identify specific criteria required for a given behavior to occur.
source: One benefit of an analytic expression is that it can be utilized to determine the generality of a result and/or to identify specific criteria required for a given behavior to occur.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of analytic expressions.

claim: The first mathematical model focuses on RAF CA and RAF dimerization.
source: Our first mathematical model focuses on RAF CA and RAF dimerization (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a description of the model with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The model allows RAF to adopt two different conformations: one is autoinhibited and can neither dimerize nor bind drug, and the other is non-autoinhibited and can bind drug and/or dimerize.
source: The model allows RAF to adopt two different conformations: one is autoinhibited and can neither dimerize nor bind drug, and the other is non-autoinhibited and can bind drug and/or dimerize (Lavoie et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a description of the model assumptions, with a citation.

claim: Drug-bound RAF is assumed to only be able to transition back to an autoinhibited state only after the bound drug has dissociated.
source: Drug-bound RAF is assumed to only be able to transition back to an autoinhibited state only after the bound drug has dissociated.
evidence: This is a description of a model assumption.

claim: Within the model, wild-type RAF is implicitly assumed to be activated by RAS-GTP as binding to RAS-GTP is an essential step to wild-type RAF activation.
source: Within the model, wild-type RAF is implicitly assumed to be activated by RAS-GTP as binding to RAS-GTP is an essential step to wild-type RAF activation (Lavoie and Therrien, 2015).
evidence: This is a description of a model assumption, with a citation.

claim: Active RAF is defined as the RAF protomers that are not bound to a drug and are part of a RAF dimer.
source: We define active RAF as the RAF protomers that are not bound to a drug and are part of a RAF dimer.
evidence: This is a definition used in the model.

claim: The mechanism shown in Figure 2A can be converted to a set of equations that provide the system's equilibrium solutions.
source: The mechanism shown in Figure 2A and its conversion to a set of equations that provide the system's equilibrium solutions is detailed in Appendix 1.
evidence: This is a description of the mathematical analysis, with reference to Figure 2A and Appendix 1.

claim: The principle of detailed balance and total protein and drug conservation equations were used to derive closed-form, analytic expressions for the steady-state solution for this system.
source: We use the principle of detailed balance (Kholodenko, 2015; Wofsy et al., 1992) and total protein and drug conservation equations to derive closed-form, analytic expressions for the steady-state solution for this system (Table 1, with derivations in Appendix 1).
evidence: This is a description of the mathematical methods used, with citations.

claim: The focus is on steady-state solutions because PA is a steady-state phenomenon.
source: We focus on steady-state solutions because PA is a steady-state phenomenon, as is reflected in the long-term outgrowth of secondary tumors with RAS mutations from patients treated with a RAF inhibitor (Su et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a justification for the modeling approach, with a citation.

claim: The presence of both CA and stabilization of the active form by RAF inhibitors is sufficient to create PA for some, but not all, parameter values.
source: We can demonstrate analytically that the presence of both CA and stabilization of the active form by RAF inhibitors is sufficient to create PA for some, but not all, parameter values (Figure 2B, Table 1, Appendix 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analytical modeling, with references to Figure 2B, Table 1, and Appendix 1.

claim: Algebraic expressions were derived that define the conditions necessary for PA to occur by the CA mechanism.
source: Additionally, our analysis yields algebraic expressions that define the conditions necessary for PA to occur by this mechanism (Table 1).
evidence: This is a description of the analytical results, with reference to Table 1.

claim: One condition for PA to occur is that RAF states must favor the autoinhibited form of RAF at equilibrium and in the absence of a drug.
source: One condition we find is that RAF states must favor the autoinhibited form of RAF at equilibrium and in the absence of a drug for PA to occur.
evidence: This is a specific condition derived from the analytical modeling.

claim: PA does not always happen when CA is present.
source: In other words, PA does not always happen when CA is present.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analytical modeling.

claim: PA can be predicted for a wide range of RAF concentration values by substituting biophysical parameter values into the derived expressions.
source: By substituting biophysical parameter values into these expressions, we can predict PA for a wide range of RAF concentration values and visualize the range of system parameters for which CA promotes PA (Figure 2C and D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a description of numerical modeling results, with references to figures.

claim: PA is not generated by simpler mechanisms such as one without the autoinhibitory conformational changes and one without dimerization.
source: In our investigations, we also analytically show that PA is not generated by simpler mechanisms such as one without the autoinhibitory conformational changes and one without dimerization (Appendix 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analytical modeling, with reference to Appendix 1.

claim: Before a drug is given, a significant fraction of RAF is autoinhibited and there are low levels of non-autoinhibited RAF and RAF dimers.
source: Before a drug is given, a significant fraction of RAF is autoinhibited and there are low levels of non-autoinhibited RAF and RAF dimers.
evidence: This is a description of the model behavior at baseline.

claim: As RAF inhibitor levels increase, the level of autoinhibited RAF progressively declines.
source: As RAF inhibitor levels increase, the level of autoinhibited RAF progressively declines.
evidence: This is a description of the model behavior with increasing drug.

claim: Non-autoinhibited RAF distributes between drug-bound monomeric and dimeric forms while the unbound monomeric form maintains equilibrium with the autoinhibited RAF.
source: Non-autoinhibited RAF distributes between drug-bound monomeric and dimeric forms while the unbound monomeric form maintains equilibrium with the autoinhibited RAF.
evidence: This is a description of the model behavior.

claim: The increased quantity of RAF dimers reflects the increased pool of RAF proteins that are non-autoinhibited and therefore capable of dimerization.
source: The increased quantity of RAF dimers reflects the increased pool of RAF proteins that are non-autoinhibited and therefore capable of dimerization.
evidence: This is an explanation of the model behavior.

claim: A drug-dependent increase in RAF dimers bound to drug in one site accounts for the increase in total RAF kinase activation that is associated with PA.
source: This results in a drug-dependent increase in RAF dimers bound to drug in one site and thereby the increase in total RAF kinase activation that accounts for PA.
evidence: This is an explanation of how PA arises in the model.

claim: The quantity of drug-bound RAF monomer and doubly drug-bound RAF dimer progressively increases to saturation as a function of the drug amount, resulting in the eventual reduction in RAF kinase activity that is associated with PA dose–responses.
source: The quantity of drug-bound RAF monomer and doubly drug-bound RAF dimer progressively increases to saturation as a function of the drug amount, resulting in the eventual reduction in RAF kinase activity that is associated with PA dose–responses.
evidence: This is an explanation of the model behavior at high drug concentrations.

claim: There is evidence that NC and RAF inhibitor-driven DP also contribute to PA.
source: There is evidence that NC and RAF inhibitor-driven DP also contribute to PA.
evidence: This is a statement about existing evidence.

claim: Previous theoretical work on PA has focused on the contribution of DP and NC.
source: Previous theoretical work on PA has focused on the contribution of DP and NC (Kholodenko, 2015; Rukhlenko et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous theoretical work.

claim: A mathematical model was developed that combined the mechanisms of CA, NC, and inhibitor-driven DP.
source: We developed a mathematical model that combined the mechanisms studied in these previous studies with our model of CA; the complete mechanism that is modeled is shown in Figure 3A, and we adapt the same nomenclature for parameters (Kholodenko, 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the unified model, with reference to Figure 3A and a citation.

claim: The three mechanisms (CA, NC, and inhibitor-driven DP) are mathematically distinct, in that one cannot translate or rescale variables to interchange between the mechanisms.
source: Analysis of our model with CA, NC, and inhibitor-driven DP finds that these three mechanisms are mathematically distinct, in that one cannot translate or rescale variables to interchange between the mechanisms (Table 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, with reference to Table 1.

claim: Each mechanism brings a qualitatively distinct feature to the dose–response of active RAF protomers.
source: Further, each mechanism brings a qualitatively distinct feature to the dose–response of active RAF protomers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B) and widely diverging capacity to potentiate the fold change in PA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) and the width of PA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling, with references to figures.

claim: A mathematical model that includes these biochemically, mathematically, and qualitatively distinct mechanisms may enable the underlying mechanisms of PA to be inferred through computationally fitting the model to data.
source: Because of these differences, we reasoned that a mathematical model that includes these biochemically, mathematically, and qualitatively distinct mechanisms may enable the underlying mechanisms of PA to be inferred, as in an inverse problem, through computationally fitting our model to data that characterizes the PA response of RAF inhibitors.
evidence: This is a reasoning about the utility of the model.

claim: A computational process was developed for obtaining sets of parameters that fit the model to published experimental data.
source: We developed a computational process for obtaining sets of parameters that fit our model to published experimental data (Karoulia et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a description of the parameter estimation approach, with a citation to the data source.

claim: The approach finds multiple parameter sets for the same drug that are within 10% of the error for the parameter set with the least error.
source: Our approach finds multiple parameter sets for the same drug that are within 10% of the error for the parameter set with the least error.
evidence: This is a description of the parameter estimation results.

claim: Published data characterize the PA response of SK-MEL-2 cells to nine different RAF inhibitors, each at seven different concentrations of inhibitor.
source: These published data characterize the PA response of SK-MEL-2 cells to nine different RAF inhibitors, each at seven different concentrations of inhibitor (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental data used, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Some parameters should be specific to the individual drugs (i.e., the dissociation constant for the drug binding to RAF, and the drug-induced DP and NC parameters).
source: We reasoned that some parameters should be specific to the individual drugs (i.e., the dissociation constant for the drug binding to RAF, and the drug-induced DP and NC parameters) and that some parameters should be the same no matter which drug was used in the experiment (i.e., the abundance of RAF, the equilibrium constant of RAF dimerization when no drug is bound, and the CA equilibrium constant).
evidence: This is a description of the reasoning behind the parameter estimation approach.

claim: Some parameters should be the same no matter which drug was used in the experiment (i.e., the abundance of RAF, the equilibrium constant of RAF dimerization when no drug is bound, and the CA equilibrium constant).
source: We reasoned that some parameters should be specific to the individual drugs (i.e., the dissociation constant for the drug binding to RAF, and the drug-induced DP and NC parameters) and that some parameters should be the same no matter which drug was used in the experiment (i.e., the abundance of RAF, the equilibrium constant of RAF dimerization when no drug is bound, and the CA equilibrium constant).
evidence: This is a description of the reasoning behind the parameter estimation approach.

claim: Values for two key parameters, RAF abundance and RAF dimerization equilibrium constant, were set based on estimates and not fit.
source: We set values for two key parameters, RAF abundance and RAF dimerization equilibrium constant, based on estimates and do not fit them.
evidence: This is a description of the parameter estimation approach.

claim: The model has 1 global parameter (the autoinhibition equilibrium constant) and 27 drug-specific parameters, for a total of 28 parameters.
source: Of note, we have 1 global parameter (the autoinhibition equilibrium constant) and 27 drug-specific parameters. Our 28 total parameter estimates yield a model that matches the experimental data well (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a description of the model parameters, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The 28 total parameter estimates yield a model that matches the experimental data well.
source: Our 28 total parameter estimates yield a model that matches the experimental data well (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the parameter estimation, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Similar quality overall fits are obtained if RAF abundance and RAF dimerization constant are not pre-specified and are added to the other 28 parameters for parameter estimation.
source: We obtain similar quality overall fits if we do not pre-specify the RAF abundance and the RAF dimerization constant and add these two parameters to the other 28 parameters and then perform the same parameter estimation procedure (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is a description of an alternative parameter estimation approach, with references to figures.

claim: Some parameters could be constrained to a narrow region through the parameter estimation procedure, while other parameters could vary widely and still match the same data.
source: We observed that some parameters could be constrained to a narrow region through this procedure, while other parameters could vary widely and still match the same data (Figure 3—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a description of the parameter estimation results, with references to figures.

claim: When the collection of best-fit parameters was considered, the different RAF inhibitors appeared to separate in a manner reflective of their known identity as type I, I.5, and II inhibitors.
source: Intriguingly, when we considered the collection of best-fit parameters we found the different RAF inhibitors appeared to separate in a manner reflective of their known identity as type I, I.5, and II inhibitors (Figure 3C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the parameter estimation, with references to Figure 3C and Supplementary file 1.

claim: Only the RAF inhibitor dose–response data was examined to completely characterize the drug-dependent parameters, whereas the classification of kinase inhibitors is typically made by consideration of the structure of each kinase inhibitor complex.
source: This is notable as only the RAF inhibitor dose–response data was examined to completely characterize the drug-dependent parameters, whereas the classification of kinase inhibitors is typically made by consideration of the structure of each kinase inhibitor complex (Dar and Shokat, 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the parameter estimation results, with a citation.

claim: The model finds that the different mechanisms result in qualitatively distinct features and the fit parameters suggest that these differences enable RAF inhibitors to be grouped based on respective mechanisms of action.
source: Thus, our model finds that the different mechanisms result in qualitatively distinct features and our fit parameters suggest that these differences enable RAF inhibitors to be grouped based on respective mechanisms of action.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the modeling and parameter estimation.

claim: The unified model (i.e., the version that includes all three mechanisms) fits the data much better than any of the sub-models that only included one or two of these processes.
